faqs.question: What is mineral spirits and what are its main industrial uses in Oman?
faqs.answer: Mineral spirits (also called white spirit, Stoddard solvent, or petroleum spirits) is a petroleum-derived solvent produced by distillation of crude oil in the naphtha range, typically with a boiling range of 140–200°C. It is primarily composed of aliphatic and alicyclic hydrocarbons (C7–C12) with low aromatic content in dearomatised grades. In Oman's industrial sector, mineral spirits is used as: a paint and varnish thinner and clean-up solvent for alkyd, oil-based, and epoxy coatings; a degreasing agent for metal parts, machinery, and workshop tools; a carrier solvent in polishes, lubricants, and rust preventives; and a cleaning solvent in printing, textiles, and automotive maintenance. It is the preferred solvent for cleaning spray guns, rollers, and brushes after oil-based paint application. The dearomatised grade (low benzene, low toluene content) is required for occupational exposure limit compliance in enclosed spaces. Global Chemicals LLC supplies mineral spirits in 5-litre cans to 200-litre drums and IBC for Oman industrial customers.

faqs.question: What is the flash point of mineral spirits and is it safe to use in enclosed spaces in Oman?
faqs.answer: Mineral spirits flash point varies by grade: Type 1 (low flash) has a flash point of approximately 21–30°C; Type 2 (medium flash) 32–50°C; and Type 3 (high flash, most common in Oman) above 55°C. For use in enclosed or confined spaces such as tank interiors, enclosed workshops, or poorly ventilated paint bays in Oman, the high-flash grade (above 55°C flash point) is mandatory to reduce fire and explosion risk. Even with high-flash mineral spirits, adequate ventilation must be maintained to keep vapour concentrations below the Lower Explosive Limit (LEL) and below occupational exposure limits (OEL) for petroleum distillates (typically 100–200 mg/m³ as 8-hour TWA). In Oman's hot climate, higher ambient temperatures accelerate solvent evaporation and reduce the safety margin relative to flash point, making ventilation requirements more stringent in summer. Personal protective equipment (nitrile gloves, chemical goggles, half-face respirator with organic vapour cartridges) is required. Global Chemicals LLC provides safety data sheets and application guidance for all solvent grades.

faqs.question: What is industrial kerosene used for in Oman and how does it differ from aviation fuel?
faqs.answer: Industrial kerosene (CAS 8008-20-6) is a petroleum distillate fraction with a boiling range of 150–300°C used as a fuel, solvent, and process chemical. In Oman, industrial kerosene applications include: agricultural and marine engine fuel for fishing boats and small vessels in Oman's coastal governorates; heating fuel for industrial ovens, dryers, and process heaters where natural gas is unavailable; cutting fluid and thread-cutting oil in metalworking (kerosene's low viscosity and flash point above 38°C make it safe for light machining and tapping of non-ferrous metals); carrier and diluent in paints, wood preservatives, and agricultural crop sprays; and mosquito and pest control applications. Industrial (commercial) kerosene differs from aviation turbine fuel (Jet-A1) in its more variable specification — Jet-A1 has tighter controls on freeze point, flash point, acidity, and contaminant levels to meet ASTM D1655 requirements for aircraft safety. Industrial kerosene does not meet Jet-A1 specification and must not be used as aircraft fuel. Global Chemicals LLC supplies industrial kerosene in drums and IBC for Oman.

title: Turpentine (Industrial Grade)
description: Industrial turpentine solvent for paint thinning and industrial applications.

details.longDescription:
Turpentine (CAS 8006-64-2) is the volatile oil distilled from pine resin, a clear, colourless to pale-yellow liquid made up mainly of alpha- and beta-pinene, with a boiling range of 150–180 °C, specific gravity 0.86–0.87, a flash point of 35 °C and the characteristic pine odour. Global Chemicals LLC supplies gum turpentine in technical grade from stock in Muscat in 1 L, 4 L and 20 L containers and 200 L drums for paint, furniture, printing and manufacturing customers across Oman.

Turpentine is the traditional thinner for oil-based and alkyd paints, varnishes and enamels: it dissolves the binder cleanly, evaporates at a rate that lets brush marks flow out, and leaves no residue. Painters and furniture finishers use it to thin coatings, to clean brushes and spray equipment, and in wax polishes and wood-finishing blends; restorers prefer it over petroleum thinners on heritage woodwork because it was the original solvent of the finishes they are repairing. Artists' paints and mediums use a rectified grade. In manufacturing it is a solvent for resins and printing inks, a degreaser, and the raw material from which pinene-based aroma chemicals, synthetic camphor and polyterpene resins are made. Compared with mineral spirits it has stronger solvency and a faster, more fragrant evaporation; compared with naphtha it is slower and less aggressive on plastics.

Handling: turpentine is flammable (flash point 35 °C) and a skin sensitiser, and its vapour irritates eyes and airways. Store it closed, cool and away from oxidisers and ignition sources; it oxidises slowly in air and thickens if left open. Earth drums during transfer, wear nitrile gloves and goggles, and ventilate spray and finishing areas. Every pack carries a specification sheet and a GHS safety data sheet.

title: Naphtha (Industrial Grade)
description: Industrial naphtha solvent for cleaning, dilution, and chemical processing.

details.longDescription:
Industrial naphtha (petroleum naphtha, CAS 64742-89-8) is a clear, colourless hydrocarbon solvent cut from crude distillation, supplied by Global Chemicals LLC in light, medium and heavy grades with boiling ranges within 30–200 °C, flash points from −4 °C to 38 °C and aromatic content of 10–25% depending on the grade, to ASTM specifications. It ships from stock in Muscat in 20 L and 200 L drums, 1,000 L IBCs, ISO tanks and bulk.

Choosing the grade. Light naphtha evaporates fastest and is the cleaning and degreasing solvent of metal-fabrication shops, engine-component cleaning and the manufacturing tenants of Sohar Industrial Port, where it leaves no residue on parts. Medium grades (the VM&P naphtha of the paint trade) thin alkyd and oil-based coatings and are the diluent in adhesives, sealants and gravure printing inks. Heavy naphtha, slower and stronger, dissolves rubber, bitumen and asphalt in tyre and rubber compounding, roofing and road-material processing. Aromatic content sets solvency: higher aromatics dissolve more resin but carry more odour and a lower exposure limit. As a feedstock, naphtha is reformed into benzene, toluene and xylene and cracked into olefins at refinery and petrochemical complexes; our supply is the solvent grade for industrial users rather than refinery-scale feedstock. A separate oilfield grade is listed under solvent naphtha.

Handling: naphtha is highly flammable (UN 1268, Class 3) and its vapour is heavier than air, so store drums closed in a ventilated, shaded, bunded area away from ignition sources, earth and bond containers during transfer, use explosion-proof pumps and wear nitrile gloves and goggles. Avoid skin contact and keep exposure within the workplace limit for the grade. Every delivery carries a certificate of analysis giving distillation range, flash point, density and aromatics, a technical data sheet and a GHS safety data sheet.

Delivery is same day within Muscat and Rusayl Industrial Area, next day to Sohar, Salalah and Duqm, and by road across the GCC with a certificate of origin. Request a quote with the grade, boiling range, pack type and monthly volume.

title: MEK (Methyl Ethyl Ketone)
description: High-purity MEK solvent for coatings, adhesives, and industrial cleaning.

details.longDescription:
Methyl ethyl ketone (MEK, 2-butanone, C4H8O, CAS 78-93-3) is a fast-evaporating ketone solvent with strong solvency for resins, supplied by Global Chemicals LLC at 99.5% minimum purity as a clear, colourless liquid with a boiling point of 80 °C and a flash point of −9 °C, in 1 L, 4 L and 20 L containers, 200 L drums and 1,000 L IBCs from stock in Muscat and Rusayl Industrial Area.

What it dissolves. MEK is one of the strongest common solvents for vinyl, acrylic, nitrocellulose, epoxy and polyurethane resins, and it is miscible with most organic solvents, which makes it the active solvent in high-solids industrial coatings, automotive refinishing thinners, gravure and flexographic printing inks, contact adhesives for PVC and rubber, and paint strippers. It evaporates about four times faster than xylene, so coatings and inks flash off quickly in the hot, dry conditions of Oman's workshops and presses, and it leaves no residue, which is why it is the degreasing and surface-preparation solvent for aluminium before bonding and painting. In the oilfield it appears in wax-inhibitor and pipeline-pigging formulations; in manufacturing it is a dewaxing solvent, a reaction medium and an intermediate.

Handling: MEK is highly flammable (UN 1193, Class 3) with vapour heavier than air, so store drums closed, cool and bunded in a ventilated area away from ignition sources and oxidisers, earth and bond containers during transfer, and use explosion-proof equipment. It defats skin and irritates eyes and airways; wear butyl or laminate gloves rather than nitrile, which MEK penetrates, plus goggles, and keep vapour within the workplace exposure limit. It softens many plastics, so use metal or HDPE containers, never PVC. Every delivery carries a certificate of analysis giving purity, water content and colour, a technical data sheet and a GHS safety data sheet.

Delivery is same day within Muscat and Rusayl, next day to Sohar, Salalah and Duqm, and by road across the GCC with a certificate of origin. Request a quote with the pack size and monthly volume; for slower, milder solvents see our mineral spirits and naphtha pages.

faqs.question: What is MEK solvent and where is it used in Oman?
faqs.answer: MEK (methyl ethyl ketone, butanone, CAS 78-93-3) is a fast-evaporating ketone solvent used in coatings, adhesives, printing inks, and chemical manufacturing. In Oman's construction and industrial sector, MEK is primarily used as: a surface preparation and cleaning solvent before epoxy or polyurethane coating application (MEK wipe test per SSPC-SP1 is standard for ensuring metal surfaces are free of oil before coating); a solvent for contact cement and PVC adhesives (including UPVC pipe joining compound in plumbing and infrastructure projects); a diluent in industrial coatings, vinyl lacquers, and nitrocellulose coatings; and a solvent in printing inks for flexible packaging. MEK has excellent solvency for resins, oils, fats, and many polymer systems while evaporating quickly enough to allow rapid coating curing. Its flash point is approximately −9°C (flammable liquid Class IB), requiring careful handling and ATEX-compliant equipment in Oman's industrial environments. Global Chemicals LLC supplies MEK in 20-litre cans, 200-litre drums, and IBCs for Oman industrial customers.
